propositions.text: The claimant is an Indian citizen.
The claimant bases his claim on section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is an Indian citizen and bases his claim on section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the IRPA, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: A friend of the claimant's brother named XXXX had police problems in 2011 due to suspected terrorist ties.
Police turned to the claimant's brother when XXXX left the country.

paragraphs.summary: A friend of the claimant's brother had police problems in 2011 and police then turned to the claimant's brother, according to the claimant.

propositions.text: The claimant's brother left India for the US in 2011 due to police pressure.
Police then targeted other claimant family members.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant says his brother left India for the US in 2011 due to police pressure, who then targeted other family members.

propositions.text: The claimant came to Canada in 2011 to participate in XXXX XXXX XXXX and then returned to India.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant came to Canada in 2011 for XXXX XXXX XXXX and then returned to India, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: In 2011, the claimant was arrested and detained for XXXX days by police accusing him of militant ties abroad.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant says he was arrested and detained in 2011 for alleged militant ties abroad.

propositions.text: The claimant went to Delhi to wait to leave India, arrived in Canada in 2012, and claimed refugee protection two weeks later.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant went to Delhi, then arrived in Canada in 2012 and claimed refugee protection two weeks later, per the claimant.

propositions.text: The claimant fears returning to India because he believes police still want to pursue him.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant fears returning to India because he believes police still want to pursue him, as stated by the claimant.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant is not a Convention refugee under section 96 of IRPA.
The panel finds the claimant is not a person in need of protection under subsection 97(1) of IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity based on documents including his passport.

paragraphs.summary: The panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity based on documents including his passport.

propositions.text: The panel noted points undermining the claimant's credibility from his testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The panel noted points undermining the claimant's credibility from his testimony.

propositions.text: The claimant said XXXX, a Muslim friend of his brother, had police problems starting in 2011.
They all lived in the same village with around XXXX residents.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said a Muslim friend of his brother had police problems from 2011 and they lived in a village with XXXX residents.

propositions.text: The police accused XXXX of terrorist ties and harassed the claimant's brother to get information.
The claimant's father paid bribes to release XXXX at least three times.
The pressure caused XXXX to leave India for the US in 2010.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said police accused XXXX of terrorist ties, harassed his brother, his father paid bribes, and XXXX left India for the US in 2010.

propositions.text: After XXXX left, police targeted the claimant's family with operations involving vehicles, questioning, searching, and mistreatment.
The claimant's father paid bribes each time for police to leave.
The claimant was present for at least two operations and was questioned about XXXX and terrorists' plans.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said police targeted his family with operations, his father paid bribes, and he was questioned about XXXX and terrorists' plans.

propositions.text: The claimant came to Canada in 2011 for XXXX XXXX XXXX and stayed about three days without claiming refugee protection.
He returned to India because he had no intention to stay in Canada.
He acknowledged his brother sought refuge in the US but said he had no direct problems.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said he came to Canada in 2011 for XXXX XXXX XXXX, stayed three days without claiming protection, then returned to India, acknowledging his brother sought refuge in the US.

propositions.text: The claimant said he was arrested and detained for XXXX days in 2011.
The claimant hesitated and delayed when asked about other arrests.
He admitted other arrests but said he forgot to include them in his PIF due to focusing on one arrest.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said he was arrested in 2011, hesitated about other arrests, then admitted them but said he forgot to include them in his PIF.

propositions.text: The claimant stayed in Delhi for six months waiting for documents to return to Canada without problems because he was in hiding.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said he stayed in Delhi six months waiting for documents without problems because he was in hiding.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant's failure to claim refugee protection in 2011 inconsistent with fearing for his life.
It finds implausible that the claimant returned home without feeling targeted despite police harassment of his family.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's failure to claim protection in 2011 inconsistent with fear and finds his return home implausible given police harassment.

propositions.text: The panel does not believe the failure to mention two arrests in the PIF was an oversight.
It considers this an attempt to embellish his story during the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The panel does not believe the failure to mention two arrests was an oversight but an attempt to embellish his story.

propositions.text: The panel considers the claimant's six-month stay in Delhi without problems indicates police are not interested in him outside his village.

paragraphs.summary: The panel considers the claimant's six-month problem-free stay in Delhi indicates police are not interested in him outside his village.

propositions.text: The panel draws a negative inference from these points affecting its analysis of an internal flight alternative in Delhi.

paragraphs.summary: The panel draws a negative inference from these points affecting its analysis of an internal flight alternative in Delhi.

propositions.text: The test for a flight alternative is two-pronged: safe relocation location and unreasonableness of expecting claimant to relocate there.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the two-pronged test for a flight alternative: safe relocation and unreasonableness of expecting relocation.

propositions.text: Claimant says returning to Delhi or Mumbai requires registration, risking police knowing personal info and danger.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant says returning to Delhi or Mumbai risks police knowing his personal info and danger due to registration.

propositions.text: The panel does not agree with the claimant's concerns about danger upon return.

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees with the claimant's concerns about danger upon return.

propositions.text: Claimant's story: local police interested in brother, family, and him; bribes paid multiple times.
Claimant explains police harassment is a business to get money through bribes.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant says local police were interested in his family and took bribes, explaining harassment as a business.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to show Delhi is unsafe for relocation.
Unlikely local authorities would search for claimant after three years, given prior bribes.
Claimant's claim that registration would alert corrupt village authorities is speculative and unsupported.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant failed to prove Delhi unsafe, doubts authorities would search after three years, and finds registration risk speculative.

propositions.text: Claimant's family still lives in Haryana state three years later.
Claimant says family moved community due to harassment by local authorities.
Claimant's explanation about family living in Haryana despite harassment indicates claimant could relocate elsewhere.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant's family still lives in Haryana; claimant alleges harassment; court finds this shows claimant could relocate elsewhere.

propositions.text: Panel rejects claimant's refugee protection claim for all stated reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the claimant's refugee protection claim for all stated reasons.
